claim: Stock WSL2 on the team's machine (WSL 2.6.1.0, kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2) loads sch_netem, sch_htb, sch_fq_codel, ifb, cls_flower, cls_fw, act_mirred and runs a netns+veth+HTB+netem testbed with IPv4 and IPv6, but has no sch_cake or sch_pie.
evidence: The primary source (Microsoft's official WSL2-Linux-Kernel repo, arch/x86/configs/config-wsl) matches the claim exactly at the specific tag the team is running. Tag linux-msft-wsl-6.6.87.2: CONFIG_NET_SCH_NETEM=m, CONFIG_NET_SCH_HTB=m, CONFIG_NET_SCH_FQ_CODEL=m, CONFIG_IFB=m, CONFIG_NET_CLS_FLOWER=m, CONFIG_NET_CLS_FW=m, CONFIG_NET_ACT_MIRRED=m, CONFIG_NET_SCH_INGRESS=m, CONFIG_NET_CLS_ACT=y, CONFIG_VETH=y, CONFIG_NET_NS=y, CONFIG_IPV6=y, CONFIG_MODULES=y; and '# CONFIG_NET_SCH_CAKE is not set', '# CONFIG_NET_SCH_PIE is not set' (CONFIG_NET_SCH_FQ_PIE absent entirely). CONFIG_LOCALVERSION="-microsoft-standard-WSL2" matches the reported uname. The same values hold on the linux-msft-wsl-6.6.y branch tip (the URL offered as support) and on the linux-msft-wsl-6.18.y branch, which is what the current latest WSL (3.0.3, released 9 Oct 2026, 'Update Microsoft.WSL.Kernel to 6.18.54.1') ships, so teammates on newer WSL get the same module set. The only divergence found is on the old 5.15.y kernel (inbox/pre-2.x WSL): there NETEM, HTB, IFB and CLS_FW are NOT set (fq_codel, flower, mirred built-in =y), so a teammate on a very old, never-updated WSL would lack HTB/netem/ifb. Note also that =m modules require WSL's modules VHD (kernelModules in .wslconfig); stock Store WSL 2.x/3.x ships it. Kernel 6.6.87.2 was introduced in WSL 2.5.9 (per release-note reposts); WSL 2.6.1 release page itself does not name the kernel, so the 2.6.1 <-> 6.6.87.2 pairing rests on the team's own uname output, which is consistent with the tag's LOCALVERSION. Runtime behaviour (actually loading the modules and running the testbed) was not independently verified here beyond the config; it rests on the team's empirical test.
correction: Claim is accurate as stated. Precision additions: (1) the module set (netem/htb/fq_codel/ifb/flower/fw/mirred as =m; cake and pie not built; fq_pie not even present) is identical across the 6.6.87.2 tag, the 6.6.y branch tip, and the 6.18.y branch used by WSL 3.0.x (kernel 6.18.54.1), so any teammate on Store-updated WSL 2.5.9+ through 3.0.3 should have the same capabilities; (2) teammates on the legacy 5.15.y inbox kernel lack sch_htb, sch_netem, ifb and cls_fw (not set there), so 'wsl --update' is a prerequisite; (3) the =m modules depend on WSL's modules VHD being present, which stock WSL ships but a custom 'kernel=' in .wslconfig without 'kernelModules=' would break.
impact_on_candidate: Low risk. The 'develop and demo on Windows laptops via WSL2' plan is supported by Microsoft's own kernel config for the exact kernel in use and for the newest WSL 3.0.x kernel. The plan should add one guardrail: require teammates to run 'wsl --update' (kernel 6.6.x or 6.18.x) and verify with 'uname -r' plus 'modprobe sch_htb sch_netem ifb', since a stale 5.15 kernel lacks HTB/netem/ifb. The CAKE/PIE gap is real on every WSL kernel branch checked, so if the QoS engine wants to compare against CAKE the team must build a custom kernel/modules VHD or use a native Linux box; HTB+fq_codel is the ceiling on stock WSL.
